hints: Interpret $|z-(4+3i)|\le2$ as all points on or inside a circle on the Argand diagram.
Place the centre at $(4,3)$, use radius $2$, and draw the boundary as included.
Draw the included vertical boundary $\operatorname{Re}z=3$ and shade only the part of the disc with real coordinate at most $3$.
walkthrough:
Interpret $|z - 4 - 3\mathrm{i}| \leqslant 2$ geometrically:
This is $|z - (4 + 3\mathrm{i})| \leqslant 2$, which represents the closed disc with centre at $(4, 3)$ and radius $2$.

Determine key boundaries of the disc:
The centre is $(4, 3)$. The circle extends horizontally from $x = 2$ to $x = 6$, and vertically from $y = 1$ to $y = 5$.

Interpret the second condition $\operatorname{Re}z \leqslant 3$:
This restricts points to the half-plane lying on or to the left of the vertical line $x = 3$.

Shade the region of intersection:
Draw the circle with centre $(4, 3)$ and radius $2$, draw the vertical line $x = 3$, and shade the region inside the circle that lies to the left of $x = 3$ (including both solid boundaries).

hints: The greatest argument is obtained on the ray from the origin that just touches the circular boundary of the region.
Join the origin to the centre $(4,3)$: its angle is $\tan^{-1}(3/4)$ and its length is $5$.
Use the right triangle formed by the radius $2$ to find the extra angle between the centre line and the upper tangent, then add the two angles.
walkthrough: Consider the argument of points on the circle with centre $C(4, 3)$ and radius $r = 2$:

Calculate the distance from the origin to the centre $C$:
$$OC = \sqrt{4^2 + 3^2} = \sqrt{25} = 5$$

Find the inclination of $OC$ from the positive real axis:
$$\theta_0 = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right) \approx 0.643501 \text{ radians}$$

Calculate the angular radius of the circle as seen from the origin:
$$\alpha = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{r}{OC}\right) = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2}{5}\right) \approx 0.411517 \text{ radians}$$

Find the argument of the upper tangent line from the origin:
$$\theta_{\text{tangent}} = \theta_0 + \alpha = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right) + \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2}{5}\right) \approx 0.643501 + 0.411517 = 1.055018 \text{ radians}$$

Verify that the point of tangency satisfies $x \leqslant 3$:
The distance to the tangent point is $OT = \sqrt{OC^2 - r^2} = \sqrt{25 - 4} = \sqrt{21} \approx 4.5826$.
Its $x$-coordinate is $x_T = OT\cos(\theta_{\text{tangent}}) = \sqrt{21}\cos(1.055018) \approx 2.26 \leqslant 3$, so the point lies inside the region.

Round the greatest argument to 2 decimal places:
$$\text{Greatest } \arg z = 1.06 \text{ radians} \quad (\text{or } 60.5^\circ)$$
